correctness.rationale: Final repaired claim. In the frozen original the main infinite-time theorem is correct, but the extension in Assumptions said absorption is 'immediate' when every configuration is monitored. For instance n=3,k=2,r=2 with Γ=γI gives survival e^(−γt), disproving immediate absorption. In the repaired RESULT.md, the norm derivative equals −⟨ψ,Γψ⟩ for arbitrary Hermitian coherent dynamics. When all vertices are monitored this lies between −γ_max||ψ||² and −γ_min||ψ||². Integration gives the two stated bounds, a zero limit and strictly positive finite-time survival. In the nontrivial domain, a boundary row belonging to a k-set meeting exactly one monitored coordinate is J times a row of the (k−1)-to-k inclusion matrix D on the m=n−r unmonitored labels. More heavily monitored rows are zero. The kernel is exactly ker D, independent of r at fixed m. I rechecked the adjacency Gram identity entrywise: diagonal k, off-diagonal 1 if the intersection has size k−1 and 0 otherwise. Thus each kernel vector extended by zero is an eigenvector at −Jk. Conversely, factoring the imaginary part of the eigenvalue against its eigenvector forces any real-energy eigenvector to vanish on monitored vertices, thence belong to that kernel. This space reduces the operator, acting as the same real scalar under its adjoint, and Jordan blocks on the orthogonal complement still decay. Hence survival is the squared norm of the dark projection, including for coherent inputs and starting monitored basis vectors. The Boolean add/remove commutator is obtained by canceling each single replacement in the two orders; their diagonal difference is m−2ℓ. Injectivity of the up-map below half rank gives surjectivity of D when k≤(m+1)/2; complementing gives injectivity when k>(m+1)/2, including m=k. Binomial rank-nullity then gives the dark dimension; the permutation-invariant projector has constant diagonal (regardless of whether the loss operator is symmetric). The binomial ratio is k/(m−k+1), and absence of dark vectors is exactly m≤2k−1. The coherent uniform state is in ran D*, so is completely absorbed. The seven independent exact SymPy instances (`python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 4`) and the independent Fraction rank/Gram replay across 83 nontrivial cases through n=8 corroborate the algebra; neither proves decay for every detector perturbation. Inspection of frozen check.py gives 83×5+24+4=443 numerical checks including four sampled real-symmetric detector perturbations, not arbitrary perturbations as numerical examples. Both corrected files distinguish these finite checks from the theorem for all Hermitian perturbations; the frozen script was not executed and its recorded numerical error is reported as recorded. The repaired VERIFICATION.md preserves the original JSON front matter verbatim.
residual_risks: Infinite-time certainty is not a uniform finite-time performance guarantee. None of the proof extends to extra unmonitored Hamiltonian terms or arbitrary dephasing.

value.rationale: The repaired claim gives the minimal placement budget for eventually absorbing every coherent input in a fixed-excitation all-to-all model. It uses the natural observable of whether any designated site is occupied; a class-wide threshold and closed input-dependent limiting law are different from the generic existence of dark states or a single numerical projector entry. The placement reduction explains why increasing the monitored set affects the limit through its reduction of the unmonitored set, not through detector rates; below threshold any dark state defeats capture even though the underlying graph remains connected. The complete-masking timing correction and special-case overlap discussion do not change this scientific contribution.
residual_risks: Exact placement statement for finite graphs and infinite-time no-jump absorption only, not an experimental time-scale or robustness result outside the specified detector sector.
